public.title: HTML Sanitizer
public.description: input is a parsed HTML-like tree, either a text string or {tag,attrs,children}. Only p, b, i, a and div elements are retained; any other tag and its entire subtree are removed. Retained elements discard all attributes except href on a, retained only when starting with https:// or /. Text and retained href are HTML-escaped (ampersand, less/greater signs, double/single quotes). Emit lowercase paired tags and no whitespace beyond source text. This is a restricted tree serializer, not a security sanitizer for arbitrary HTML source. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, fixtures and reference solutions, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party exercise text or implementation copied.

explanation: Recursively allowlist tags and attributes, discard forbidden subtrees, and escape output values. O(n plus output length) time and space; parsing and browser security are outside this limited adapter. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
